content.text:
I have what I need. Let me confirm the finding.

**Analysis:**

- **§ 3.19 (p0369–p0374) "Exclusivity Commitment of SFJ"** — the sole exclusivity/competing-product restraint in the agreement, and it binds **SFJ**, not us: "*SFJ shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to...*" It restrains SFJ from clinical trials of, or selling, Competing Products and Brilinta Competing Products during the Exclusive Period (p0085: to Nov 21, 2022 / Nov 21, 2024). This **benefits PB** — per detection guidance, "Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine," and we must not flag it.
- **"Competing Product" / "Brilinta Competing Product" (p0057, p0029)** appear *only* in SFJ's own covenant — there is no reciprocal definition or restraint applied to PB.
- **PB-side negative covenants (§ 7.5, p0545–p0557)** are financing covenants — indebtedness, liens/encumbrances on PB Intellectual Property, dividends/Prohibited Investments, sales of royalty streams, further negative pledges. None restricts what businesses PB may operate or what products PB may develop, buy or build.
- **§ 7.5.5 Licensing Transactions (p0552)** is a consent right over out-licensing the funded Product, with an Excluded Licensing Transaction carve-out and an expedited arbitration challenge (p0553–p0554). This is a collateral-protection provision tied to the financed asset, not a non-compete or field-of-use restriction on competing products — and it is a distinct commercial term I should not double-flag here.
- Searches for "shall not develop/engage", "field of use", "compete", "exclusivity" surfaced no PB-side restraint.

No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds PB, so this sits at the **preferred** position and requires no redline.

input.quote: 3.19 Exclusivity Commitment of SFJ. During the applicable Exclusive Period, SFJ shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, either by itself or through a Third Party, conduct human clinical trials of, or sell, offer for sale or have sold:
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on PB, so it meets the preferred position (no restriction on Customer). The only exclusivity/competing-product covenant is § 3.19 (p0369–p0374), which runs one way against SFJ and its Affiliates during the Exclusive Period (p0085), and therefore benefits us — per the rule's detection guidance, restrictions binding the counterparty are acceptable and are not flagged. The "Competing Product" and "Brilinta Competing Product" definitions (p0057, p0029) are used only in SFJ's covenant; there is no reciprocal restraint on PB. Searches for "shall not develop/engage in", "field of use", "compete" and "exclusivity" returned no PB-side restraint. The PB-side negative covenants in § 7.5 (p0545–p0557) are financing/collateral covenants (indebtedness, liens on PB Intellectual Property, distributions and Prohibited Investments, sales of royalty streams, further negative pledges) and do not limit the businesses PB may operate or the products PB may buy or build. Noted but not flagged here: § 7.5.5 (p0552) gives SFJ a consent right over non-Excluded Licensing Transactions, which constrains our licensing freedom; it is a collateral-protection term tied to the funded Product rather than a competing-product or field-of-use restraint, it carries an Excluded Licensing Transaction carve-out and an expedited arbitration challenge (p0553–p0554), and it belongs to a separate commercial term that should not be double-flagged under this rule. No redline proposed.
